description: The MoodVerse controlled taxonomy. Closed, versioned, religion-neutral vocabularies used by the enrichment layer. Independent of any source dataset's terminology. Values are stable snake_case identifiers safe for use as database enums and JSON-schema enum members; display labels may change without a data migration, identifiers may not.

versioning_policy.minor_bump: Adding a value to any axis. Existing annotations remain valid.
versioning_policy.major_bump: Removing a value, or changing what an existing value means. Requires re-annotation of every affected record.
versioning_policy.identifier_stability: An id is never reused for a different concept. A retired id is tombstoned, never recycled.

design_notes.two_axis_emotion_use: The `emotions` vocabulary is used on TWO distinct record axes and they are never interchangeable. `expressed_affect` is the emotional register OF THE TEXT - this is where every source emotion label maps. `addressed_states` is the set of user emotional states the verse is a FIT RESPONSE TO - this is what retrieval joins against, and no source dataset measures it. See mapping_rules.md for the build-time assertion that enforces the separation.
design_notes.why_this_matters: Measured against the Phase 0 corpus: Complete_Quran_data emotion label `Fear` co-occurs with judgment/punishment content in 1614 of 1823 assignments (89%), `Sadness` in 93%, `Anger at Injustice` in 94%. Source emotion labels describe what the text expresses, not who it helps. Collapsing the two axes into one field would serve 1614 punishment verses to frightened users.
design_notes.valence_free_themes: Themes carry no valence. `afterlife_punishment` is as legitimate a theme as `divine_mercy`. Keeping subject matter separate from suitability is what allows a verse to be described accurately and still excluded from default recommendation.

emotions.definition: A felt emotional state, as a person would name it about themselves, at the granularity at which a scripture response can meaningfully differ.
inclusion_criteria: A user could plausibly type it about themselves.
The appropriate pastoral response differs from every other value in this list.
It is a state, not a situation, a virtue, or a request.
exclusion_criteria: Situations belong to the `situations` axis (bereavement, illness).
Spiritual acts belong to the `intents` axis (repentance, praise).
Virtues and dispositions are not emotional states (humility, faith, patience-as-virtue).
Theological postures are mapped to their emotional equivalent: 'fear of God' is `awe`, never `fear`.
Clinical diagnoses are never used. 'depression' is not a value; the situation `mental_health_struggle` plus states such as `sadness` or `despair` carry it.

values.label: Anxiety
values.definition: Anticipatory dread about an uncertain future.
excludes: fear of an identified present threat (fear)
values.boundary: vs `fear`: no identified present object. When an input names no object, choose `anxiety`.

values.label: Fear
values.definition: Fear of a present, identified threat.
values.boundary: vs `anxiety`: object-specific and immediate. Source labels rendered 'fear of Allah' or 'fear of the LORD' map to `awe`, NEVER here.

values.label: Grief
values.definition: Sorrow arising from a specific, irrecoverable loss.
includes: loss of health, home, or capacity
values.boundary: vs `sadness`: has an identifiable loss.

values.label: Sadness
values.definition: Low mood, heaviness or discouragement without a specific loss.
values.boundary: vs `grief`: no locus.

values.label: Loneliness
values.definition: Felt absence of connection, whether human or divine.
includes: being far from home or family
values.boundary: vs `sadness`: relational in content. Note the distinct situation `isolation`, which is the circumstance rather than the feeling.

values.label: Anger
values.definition: Indignation - at injustice, at another person, at circumstance, or at God.
excludes: the text's own denunciatory tone, which is expressed_affect not a user state
values.boundary: Low-intensity frustration is `anger` at intensity 1; there is no separate value for it.

values.label: Guilt
values.definition: Distress about something one DID.
values.boundary: vs `shame`: act-focused and repairable. Guilt is answered by `forgiveness` and `repentance`.

values.label: Shame
values.definition: Distress about what one IS.
values.boundary: vs `guilt`: identity-focused, and not repaired by apology. Shame is answered by `assurance`, not by `repentance`.

values.label: Despair
values.definition: Hopelessness; the belief that nothing will change.
includes: feeling there is no way out
values.boundary: vs `sadness`: forward-looking and totalising. SAFETY-CRITICAL: records addressing `despair` are prioritised for human review and are subject to the crisis rule.

values.label: Exhaustion
values.definition: Depletion, burnout, weariness.
values.boundary: vs `sadness`: a matter of capacity, not mood. Answered by `strength` and `peace`, rarely by `encouragement`.

values.label: Confusion
values.definition: Not knowing what to do; decision paralysis.
values.boundary: vs `doubt`: practical, not spiritual. Answered by `guidance` and `wisdom`.

values.label: Doubt
values.definition: Uncertainty about God, about faith, or about being heard.
values.boundary: vs `confusion`: the object is spiritual. Answered by `assurance`, and legitimately by `lament`.

values.label: Gratitude
values.definition: Thankfulness seeking expression.
excludes: worship of God for who God is (that is the intent praise)
values.boundary: vs `joy`: directed at a giver.

values.label: Joy
values.definition: Happiness, gladness, celebration.
values.boundary: vs `gratitude`: undirected.

values.label: Awe
values.definition: Wonder and reverence before greatness; the sense of one's own smallness.
includes: the sense rendered as 'fear of God' in source vocabularies
values.boundary: vs `fear`: not aversive. This is the correct target for every source label of the 'fear of Allah' / 'fear of the LORD' form.

values.label: Peace
values.definition: Settledness, calm, contentment.
excludes: absence of conflict as a circumstance
the DESIRE for peace, which is the intent `peace`
values.boundary: RESOLUTION RULE: when an input names a desired state ('I need peace'), the desired state goes to the `intents` axis and the state the person is actually in (anxiety, exhaustion, anger) goes here. `peace` is an emotional state only when the person reports currently having it.

values.label: Hope
values.definition: Forward-looking expectation of good.
excludes: wanting hope while feeling none (that is despair as state, hope as intent)
values.boundary: vs `joy`: not yet realised.

documented_ambiguities: anxiety/fear overlap in everyday speech. Rule: absent an identified object, use `anxiety`.
guilt/shame are frequently co-reported. Rule: primary is whichever the text or user names more specifically; the other becomes secondary.
peace as state vs peace as intent. Rule stated on the `peace` value above.
grief/sadness. Rule: if a loss is nameable, it is `grief`.

nuance_terms.definition: An OPEN, non-retrieval field recording shades the closed emotion vocabulary cannot carry. Never queried, never filtered on, never used in any score or curation rule.
nuance_terms.purpose: The taxonomy's measured growth path. Terms recurring above a threshold across a release become candidates for promotion into the closed `emotions` vocabulary at the next minor version bump, instead of the vocabulary growing ad hoc.

intensity.scale_rationale: Not 1-10. A 10-point scale invites annotators - human or model - to express confidence as precision, and the differences between 6 and 7 are noise that cannot be adjudicated or measured for agreement.
intensity.two_field_note: `text_intensity` is the emotional force of the verse itself. `serves_intensity` is an INTERVAL {min,max} of user intensity the verse serves well, because suitability is not monotone: 'Be still, and know that I am God' fits 1-2 and reads as dismissive at 4, while 'Out of the depths have I cried unto thee' fits 3-4 and is disproportionate at 1.

values.label: low
values.anchor: Present in the background; the person is functioning normally.

values.label: moderate
values.anchor: Clearly felt and named; functioning with effort.

values.label: high
values.anchor: Acute and dominating; hard to function.

values.label: crisis
values.anchor: Overwhelming; safety-relevant. Subject to the crisis rule.

themes.definition: What the passage is ABOUT - its subject matter.
inclusion_criteria: Applicable to both scriptures without theological commitment.
Describes subject matter, not effect on a reader.
exclusion_criteria: No emotional content - that is the `emotions` axis.
No pastoral function - that is the `intents` axis.
No speech-act - that is the `scripture_purposes` axis.
No valence. A theme never implies a verse is good or bad to recommend.

values.label: Divine presence
values.definition: God is with, near, or accompanying.

values.label: Divine mercy
values.definition: God's compassion, kindness, and pardon.

values.label: Divine power
values.definition: God's sovereignty, might, and control over creation and events.

values.label: Divine faithfulness
values.definition: God's steadfastness and keeping of promises.

values.label: Divine justice
values.definition: God's righteousness and just dealing.
values.boundary: The attribute. The outcome is `afterlife_punishment` or `accountability_and_reckoning`; a verse may carry both.

values.label: Divine guidance
values.definition: Direction, light, or teaching given by God.

values.label: Divine provision
values.definition: Sustenance, care, and needs met.

values.label: Divine knowledge
values.definition: God sees, knows, and is aware.

values.label: Human frailty
values.definition: Mortality, weakness, transience, limitation.
values.boundary: vs `suffering_and_trial`: limitation from within, not affliction from outside.

values.label: Suffering and trial
values.definition: Affliction, testing, hardship.

values.label: Sin and wrongdoing
values.definition: Transgression, moral failure.

values.label: Repentance and return
values.definition: Turning back, seeking pardon.

values.label: Doubt and questioning
values.definition: Lament, complaint, unanswered questions put to God.

values.label: Mortality and death
values.definition: Dying, the grave, the brevity of life.

values.label: Pride and humility
values.definition: Self-exaltation and lowliness.

values.label: Trust and reliance
values.definition: Dependence on God.

values.label: Prayer and supplication
values.definition: Asking, calling out, petition.

values.label: Praise and thanksgiving
values.definition: Worship and gratitude expressed.

values.label: Patience and endurance
values.definition: Steadfastness under duress.

values.label: Obedience and devotion
values.definition: Following commands; faithfulness in practice.
values.boundary: vs `covenant_and_law`: the disposition toward an obligation, not its content.

values.label: Remembrance and meditation
values.definition: Dwelling on God; recollection.

values.label: Courage and strength
values.definition: Being strong; not fearing.

values.label: Hope and expectation
values.definition: Looking forward; awaiting deliverance.

values.label: Love and compassion
values.definition: Love and mercy shown toward others.

values.label: Forgiveness between people
values.definition: Pardon extended or sought between persons.

values.label: Family and kinship
values.definition: Parents, children, spouses, relatives.

values.label: Justice toward others
values.definition: Fairness; defending the oppressed.

values.label: Speech and truthfulness
values.definition: The tongue, honesty, slander, testimony.

values.label: Generosity and charity
values.definition: Giving, alms, provision for the needy.

values.label: Wisdom and discernment
values.definition: Understanding, insight, sound judgement.

values.label: Self-restraint
values.definition: Control of appetite, anger, and desire.

values.label: Work and diligence
values.definition: Labour, effort, sloth.

values.label: Wealth and possessions
values.definition: Riches, poverty, property.

values.label: Contentment and simplicity
values.definition: Sufficiency; freedom from craving.

values.label: Deliverance and rescue
values.definition: Being saved out of danger or distress.

values.label: Healing and restoration
values.definition: Being made whole; what was broken repaired.

values.label: Peace and rest
values.definition: Stillness, safety, repose.

values.label: Renewal and new beginning
values.definition: Starting again; being made new.

values.label: Afterlife reward
values.definition: Paradise, recompense for the righteous.

values.label: Afterlife punishment
values.definition: Hell, torment, recompense for the wicked.
values.note: A neutral descriptor. Carrying this theme is not by itself an exclusion trigger; suitability and isolation risk decide that.

values.label: Accountability and reckoning
values.definition: Being answerable; the weighing of deeds.

values.label: Resurrection and final day
values.definition: The raising of the dead; the last day.

values.label: Prophetic narrative
values.definition: Stories of prophets and scriptural figures.

values.label: Covenant and law
values.definition: Legal, ritual, or covenantal prescription.
values.boundary: vs `obedience_and_devotion`: the content of an obligation, not the disposition toward it.

values.label: Revelation and scripture
values.definition: The text speaking about itself, its sending down, or its authority.

values.label: Creation and nature
values.definition: The made world; signs in nature.

values.label: Community history
values.definition: The story of a people: exile, nations, generations past.

intents.definition: The pastoral act the verse can perform FOR A READER.
inclusion_criteria: It must be something a person could be helped by receiving.
exclusion_criteria: Not the passage's own literary function - that is `scripture_purposes`.
Not the reader's emotional state - that is `emotions`.

values.label: Comfort
values.definition: Meets present pain with presence or solace.

values.label: Hope
values.definition: Points to future good.
values.distinguished_from: `encouragement`: concerns the outcome, not the effort.

values.label: Encouragement
values.definition: Bolsters someone to keep going.

values.label: Peace
values.definition: Settles agitation.

values.label: Guidance
values.definition: Says what to do, or how to see a situation.

values.label: Strength
values.definition: Supplies capacity to endure or act.

values.label: Patience
values.definition: Invites endurance while an outcome is out of one's hands.

values.label: Perseverance
values.definition: Invites continued effort against resistance.

values.label: Gratitude
values.definition: Invites thanksgiving.

values.label: Praise
values.definition: Invites worship and adoration.

values.label: Repentance
values.definition: Invites turning from one's own wrong.

values.label: Forgiveness
values.definition: Concerns pardon received from God, or extended to another.

values.label: Wisdom
values.definition: Supplies general understanding for living.

values.label: Warning
values.definition: Admonishes; announces consequence.
values.rationale: 3446 Quran ayat (55.3%) carry judgment or punishment content. Without an honest label for it, that content is force-fitted into `guidance` and becomes recommendable. Honest labelling is what makes honest exclusion possible.

values.label: Lament
values.definition: Gives voice to pain WITHOUT resolving it.
values.rationale: Psalm 88, Lamentations, the complaint psalms. A person in acute grief is often better served by a verse that names their pain than by one that fixes it. This is a genuine pastoral act and one of the few intents safe at crisis intensity.

values.label: Assurance
values.definition: Confirms standing, identity, or security.
values.rationale: The answer to `doubt` and to `shame`, neither of which `comfort` addresses. Comfort meets pain; assurance meets the question 'am I still acceptable'.

values.label: Instruction
values.definition: Didactic or legal content: how a duty is performed.
values.rationale: A neutral home for law and ritual so it is not mislabelled as `guidance` and surfaced to someone seeking direction in distress.

documented_ambiguities: patience/perseverance overlap heavily. Tie-break: waiting (outcome outside your control) vs effort (resistance to push through). Where both genuinely apply, list both.

situations.definition: The concrete life circumstance a user is in.
inclusion_criteria: Common enough to be a useful retrieval facet.
exclusion_criteria: Emotional states belong to the `emotions` axis.
Nothing requiring inference about the user beyond what they said.
situations.sparsity_note: Sparse by design. Most verses carry 0-3; many carry none. An empty list is normal and is not a gap.

values.label: Bereavement
values.definition: Death of someone close.

values.label: Own illness
values.definition: The person's own sickness, injury or disability.

values.label: Illness of a loved one
values.definition: Sickness of someone close to them.

values.label: Mental health struggle
values.definition: A period of mental or emotional difficulty, named as a circumstance and never as a diagnosis.
values.note: MoodVerse must never present scripture as treatment. Verses tagged here are held out of crisis responses unless crisis_safe is true.

values.label: Financial hardship
values.definition: Debt, poverty, inability to meet needs.

values.label: Unemployment or work stress
values.definition: Job loss, overwork, workplace pressure.

values.label: Academic pressure
values.definition: Study, examinations, educational strain.

values.label: Relationship conflict
values.definition: Strife with a friend, relative or colleague.

values.label: Marriage difficulty
values.definition: Strain, separation or breakdown in marriage.

values.label: Parenting
values.definition: Raising children; concern for one's children.

values.label: Singleness
values.definition: Being unpartnered, whether by choice or circumstance.

values.label: Betrayal or broken trust
values.definition: Being deceived or let down by someone trusted.

values.label: Isolation
values.definition: Being cut off from community or support.
values.boundary: The circumstance. The feeling is the emotion `loneliness`.

values.label: Displacement or migration
values.definition: Exile, refuge, moving far from home.

values.label: Persecution or discrimination
values.definition: Being targeted for faith, identity or origin.

values.label: Injustice experienced
values.definition: Being wronged without redress.

values.label: Major decision
values.definition: A consequential choice to be made.

values.label: Life transition
values.definition: A significant change of stage or circumstance.

values.label: Waiting for an answer
values.definition: An unresolved situation whose outcome is pending.

values.label: Temptation struggle
values.definition: Pull toward something the person judges wrong.

values.label: Addiction struggle
values.definition: Compulsive behaviour the person wishes to stop.

values.label: Aftermath of moral failure
values.definition: Living with the consequences of one's own wrong.

values.label: Caregiving burden
values.definition: Sustained care for a dependent person.

values.label: Aging
values.definition: Growing old; declining capacity; end of life.

values.label: Conflict or war
values.definition: Armed conflict or civil violence.

values.label: Natural disaster
values.definition: Earthquake, flood, famine, storm.

values.label: Spiritual dryness
values.definition: A period when faith feels empty or absent.

values.label: Celebration or milestone
values.definition: A wedding, birth, achievement or festival.

values.label: New beginning
values.definition: A fresh start.

values.label: Moment of gratitude
values.definition: An occasion prompting thankfulness.

scripture_purposes.definition: What the passage is DOING in its own text - the speech-act axis.
scripture_purposes.why_this_axis_exists: It is the strongest single predictor of context dependency and of misleading-if-isolated, and no Phase 0 source annotates it for either scripture.
exclusion_criteria: Not what the verse can do for a reader - that is `intents`.
scripture_purposes.context_dependency_prior_scale: low | medium | high - a PRIOR only. It may shift an assessed context_dependency by at most one ordinal level and never originates one.

values.label: Declaration about God
values.definition: States who God is or what God does.

values.label: Promise
values.definition: Commits to future good.
values.note: An `addressee_specific` promise made to one named person or nation must never be served as though made to the reader. Such records reach INCLUDE_WITH_CONTEXT at best.

values.label: Command
values.definition: Instructs the hearer to do something.

values.label: Prohibition
values.definition: Instructs the hearer not to do something.

values.label: Legal ruling
values.definition: Prescriptive law or ritual regulation.

values.label: Warning or threat
values.definition: Announces consequence for conduct.

values.label: Narrative event
values.definition: Recounts what happened.

values.label: Reported speech
values.definition: A character speaks within the text.
values.note: The single largest source of misleading-if-isolated content. A verse may accurately record what an adversary, a fool, a false comforter or a despairing person said. Psalm 14:1 reads 'The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God' - the isolated clause inverts the passage. 4857 AKJV verses (15.6%) contain a speech verb, so this surface is large.

values.label: Lament or complaint
values.definition: Voiced pain or protest addressed to God.

values.label: Praise or thanksgiving
values.definition: Worship or thanks offered.

values.label: Prayer or supplication
values.definition: Petition addressed to God.

values.label: Wisdom saying
values.definition: A proverb or aphorism.

values.label: Prophecy or oracle
values.definition: A declared word about what is or will be.

values.label: Genealogy or record
values.definition: Lists, censuses, measurements, registers.
values.note: Low context dependency and low standalone usefulness simultaneously - nothing is missing, and nothing is there. This pair is why the two scores must stay separate.

values.label: Exhortation
values.definition: An argued appeal to act or believe.

values.label: Question or rhetorical
values.definition: Poses a question, often not to be answered.

values.label: Blessing or benediction
values.definition: Pronounces good upon someone.

values.label: Oath or covenant
values.definition: A binding undertaking or its terms.
Holds without a stated condition.
Holds only if a stated condition is met. Displaying the apodosis without the protasis is an isolation risk.
Made to a named person, group or nation. Not transferable to the reader without context.
God speaks.
A prophet, messenger or apostle speaks.
A figure the text presents approvingly speaks.
The text's own narrating voice.
An unremarkable human speaker.
An opponent, a fool, a deceiver, or a figure the text presents as wrong.
The speaker cannot be determined from the verse alone.

context_dependency.definition: How much surrounding text the plain meaning of the verse requires.
context_dependency.reasons_note: The typed reasons matter more than the number. They are what makes the level auditable, what tells the client which context to render, and what a human reviewer can disagree with specifically. `dependency_reasons` is MANDATORY at level >= 2.

values.label: self_contained
values.anchor: Full meaning available from the verse alone.

values.label: lightly_dependent
values.anchor: A connective or pronoun resolves trivially; the meaning survives isolation.

values.label: passage_dependent
values.anchor: Needs 1-3 adjacent verses.

values.label: pericope_dependent
values.anchor: Needs the surrounding unit - story, discourse, psalm, chapter.

values.label: frame_dependent
values.anchor: Needs a frame the text does not supply: who is speaking, the historical occasion, a legal system, a prior covenant.

dependency_reasons.definition: A pronoun whose referent is not in the verse.
Opens with And, But, For, Therefore, So, Then and similar.
Not a complete clause on its own.
Contains speech whose speaker the verse does not name.
The speaker is a figure the text presents as wrong.
The 'then' clause whose 'if' lies outside the verse.
A person, place or thing identified upstream.
Presupposes a legal or ritual system to make sense.
Spoken to one named individual or nation rather than to readers generally.
Requires the occasion of revelation or the historical situation. Covers asbab al-nuzul for the Quran and situational framing for the Bible under one neutral term.
A figure of speech that misleads if read literally without its frame.
Says the opposite of what it means.
One member of a list whose sense depends on the whole.

scales.design_rule: All judgement scores are integers 0-4 with named behavioural anchors. No floats. A model asked for 0.73 produces noise dressed as precision; a model choosing among five defined levels produces a decision that can be audited, disagreed with, and measured for inter-rater agreement with weighted Cohen's kappa.

standalone_usefulness.definition: Read alone, with no surrounding text, does this verse make sense and land?

values.label: unusable_alone
values.anchor: Meaning unavailable: fragment, unattributed pronoun, bare list item.

values.label: weak
values.anchor: Parseable but flat or confusing alone: genealogy, measurement, procedural detail.

values.label: serviceable
values.anchor: Understandable; unremarkable as a reflection.

values.label: strong
values.anchor: Self-contained and carries a complete thought worth reflecting on.

values.label: exemplary
values.anchor: Self-contained, complete and memorable; works as the entire response.

emotional_relevance.definition: Does this verse speak to this user state?

values.label: none
values.anchor: No bearing on the state.

values.label: tangential
values.anchor: Shares vocabulary, not substance. The word 'fear' appears, but as reverence toward God.
values.purpose: This level exists solely to give lexical and embedding false positives a place to be recorded as such. Without it they get rounded up to 'related', which is how emotionally inappropriate matches re-enter through the back door.

values.label: related
values.anchor: Touches the state indirectly.

values.label: direct
values.anchor: Speaks to the state.

values.label: precise
values.anchor: Speaks to the state's specific texture.

purpose_suitability.definition: Does this verse perform this pastoral act well?

values.label: unsuitable
values.anchor: Does not perform this act at all.

values.label: poor
values.anchor: Could be stretched to perform it, but badly.

values.label: acceptable
values.anchor: Performs it adequately.

values.label: good
values.anchor: Performs it well.

values.label: excellent
values.anchor: Performs it outstandingly; a first-choice response.

purpose_suitability.mandatory_blocker_rule: Whenever emotional_relevance >= 3 for any state AND purpose_suitability <= 1 for a given intent, at least one blocker MUST be recorded for that intent. The annotation is invalid without one. This forces the 'relevant but unsuitable' case - the core product requirement - to be explained rather than averaged away.

isolation_risk.definition: How badly does the plain isolated reading distort the passage?

values.label: none
values.anchor: Reads correctly alone.

values.label: mild
values.anchor: Loses nuance alone.

values.label: significant
values.anchor: Plausibly misread alone.

values.label: severe
values.anchor: The plain isolated reading contradicts the passage's meaning: quoted adversary speech, irony, a conditional stripped of its condition.

kinds.definition: Words of an adversary or negative exemplar read as the text's own claim.
A statement meant as its opposite.
A promise or threat separated from its condition.
A promise to a named party read as universal.
A metaphor taken at face value.
Half of a contrast or a completed thought.
A command bound to one occasion read as standing instruction.
Reads as attributing a person's suffering to their fault.

curation_confidence.definition: How much do we trust THE ANNOTATION RECORD - not the verse.
curation_confidence.note: A verse can be an excellent reflection with confidence 0.20 (annotated once, unreviewed) or a poor one with confidence 0.95. Confidence gates promotion, never quality. A model's self-reported certainty NEVER becomes this value.

bands.evidence: Single model pass, no independent corroboration, no human review.
Single model pass agreeing with at least one independent source annotation, or with a deterministic prior.
Two independent model passes agree; or one pass plus expert-tier (ELQV) agreement on expressed_affect.
A human reviewer approved the field group.
Human-approved and in the gold set with measured agreement.

blockers.definition: The verse's force is admonition or threatened consequence.
Spoken to a named person or nation, not to readers.
The good is contingent on a condition not visible in the verse.
Needs the surrounding story to mean anything.
The words are those of a figure the text presents as wrong.
Plausibly worsens the state it would be served for.
Could read as attributing the person's suffering to their fault.
For the repentance intent: contains no invitation to turn.
The available rendering is too obscure to land.
The reading is disputed; serving it asserts a position.

content_advisories.definition: Touches mental health or addiction; must never read as treatment.

structural.definition: Non-semantic descriptive fields. These carry structural facts that must not be forced onto a semantic axis.

values.definition: Revealed at Mecca, per Complete_Quran_data's context column.
Revealed at Medina, per Complete_Quran_data's context column.
No source states it for this ayah.

revelation_period.rationale: Complete_Quran_data's `context` column mixes discourse type with revelation chronology. Chronology is a structural fact about the text, not a semantic or emotional one, and is given its own field rather than being mapped onto themes or situations.

values.definition: Copied from a source annotation through an approved ledger row. Deterministic and reversible.
Computed by a stated, versioned rule from text or metadata.
Single model pass, unreviewed.
Two or more independent passes reconciled by rule; disagreements recorded, not smoothed.
A named reviewer inspected and accepted or edited it.
Human-reviewed, passed the release checklist, and assigned to a release version.

annotation_methods.monotonicity_rule: A field's method may move UP this ladder. A pipeline re-run that would move it down writes a proposal to the review queue instead of overwriting. This is what prevents a re-run from erasing human work.

values.definition: Eligible for default emotional recommendation, subject to the per-state veto and the crisis rule.
Eligible only when displayed together with its recommended context span.
Not offered as an emotional recommendation. NOT deleted - remains fully present and searchable in study, browse and reference modes.
A state, not a verdict. Awaiting human judgement. Never served. Carries a maximum age after which it is reported as stale.
